context.text: Kalimera Jordan! Tonight at 8: scene 4 of Lighthouse, Theo walking back into Mara's bar, about 200 words in 20 minutes. Send me the scene when it's done. You in?

transcript.text: [document lighthouse-scene-4.pages: Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. Mara kept the second chair.] done!

Nice, Jordan, scene 4 is written 🔥 The Pages file won't open on my end, though. Can you export it as a PDF (File > Export To > PDF) or send a screenshot of the scene? Then I can read it and give you feedback.

oh ok, here [document lighthouse-scene-4.pdf: Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. "You kept the second chair," he said. Mara shrugged, wiping a glass that was already dry. "Somebody had to."]

Got it, Jordan, and I like "You kept the second chair." The silence in that line does a lot of work 🔥 That PDF is about 30 words, though, and today's step was a 200-word scene. Is there more of scene 4 that didn't make it into the export?

checks.reason: Plainly says the Pages file won't open and offers a PDF or screenshot, but opens with "Nice... scene 4 is written", which celebrates a file it hasn't read.
Names only a PDF export or a screenshot as proof, never typed text.
Four sentences, and the one question sits mid-text, followed by "Then I can read it and give you feedback."
Warm and energetic with one emoji as punctuation, no suspicion.
Gently notes the export is far shorter than the 200-word step, though the pushback is framed as a question rather than a clear count.
Reacts to the specific line "You kept the second chair" and the silence it carries.
Four sentences, exceeding the three-sentence limit, though it has only one question at the end.
Warm, enthusiastic, one emoji as punctuation, not accusing.

conversation.reason: The PDF is never counted as proof; ZOH gives feedback and asks about more text rather than acknowledging the document as the step's proof.
ZOH reacts to the second chair and asks one question without paste, but never counts the PDF; it asks whether more of the scene exists instead.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the unopenable Pages file well, plainly asking for a PDF, screenshot or export with a clear path. But once the PDF arrived it reacted specifically to the second-chair line without counting the step, and it ran four sentences with its question not at the end.
